newsitem.title: USA: CBOT, CBOE commit millions to push Dow products.
newsitem.headline: CBOT, CBOE commit millions to push Dow products.

text.p: The Chicago Board of Trade and Chicago Board Options Exchange will spend $11 million just to prepare floor space for their proposed derivatives based on the Dow Jones Industrial Average, the heads of the two exchanges said Monday.
At a news conference, they declined to specify costs for in-house marketing and educational efforts, much less confidential licensing pact costs with Dow Jones & Co, citing competitive reasons.
But CBOT president Thomas Donovan said his exchange would spend $8 million to build a 350-person-capacity trading pit, add 100 booths and expand wallboard space to support its DJIA futures.
The CBOE will spend $3 million to modify its existing equity options pits to handle Dow-based index options business, CBOE president Charles Henry said.
"This will be the largest initiative...by several-fold (of) anything we've done before, including what was done several years ago when index options came out," said CBOE chairman William Brodsky.

At the CBOT, the expected early-October launch of futures on the DJIA reintroduces stock index products as part of the exchange's debt and agricultural contract lineup and thus will consume one-third of CBOT's marketing budget, officials said.

CBOE and CBOT also expect their Dow products, which they said face a routine regulatory approval process, to dominate the mini-Standard & Poor's 500 futures the Chicago Mercantile Exchange announced after it lost a bid for Dow-based futures.
But they said they expected DJIA futures and options to drum up new business, including intermarket arbitrage. The CBOT is working with CME on a formal cross-margining agreement.
"No one has to fail for us to succeed," added Peter Kann, chairman of Dow Jones & Co.
